title: For You Pack
description: Tiny routines for the parent alone. A steadier parent makes everything else in the week easier, so these take two or three minutes and need nothing but you.

routines.title: Reset Before Pickup
routines.description: Two quiet minutes before you see your child, so you arrive calm rather than rushed.
routines.parentGoal: Arrive at the next part of the day settled instead of carrying the last one in.
routines.childOutcome: Meets a calmer parent, which makes the first minutes together go more smoothly.
steps: Before you get out of the car or open the door, put your phone face down.
Take three slow breaths, longer out than in.
Name one thing you're looking forward to with your child today.

routines.title: Name What You Feel
routines.description: When you notice tension rising, put one word to it before you respond.
routines.parentGoal: Create a short gap between feeling and reacting.
routines.childOutcome: Gets a response instead of a reaction, and sees what it looks like to pause.
steps: Notice the signal: tight shoulders, a raised voice, a fast heartbeat.
Breathe out slowly once, then decide what to say.

routines.title: One Good Moment
routines.description: At the end of the day, write down one moment with your child that went well.
routines.parentGoal: Balance a hard day by noticing what worked, however small.
routines.childOutcome: A parent who notices good moments tends to notice more of them the next day.
steps: Before bed, think back over the day with your child.
Write one sentence about a moment that went well, even a small one.
Add what you did that helped, if anything comes to mind.

routines.title: Be Kind After a Hard Moment
routines.description: After a moment you're not proud of, speak to yourself the way you'd speak to a friend.
routines.parentGoal: Recover from a hard moment without piling on blame, so you can repair.
routines.childOutcome: A parent who isn't stuck in guilt can come back and reconnect sooner.
steps: Step away for a moment if you can.
Say to yourself: 'That was hard. I'm learning too.'
Pick one small thing you'll do to reconnect when you're ready.

routines.title: Drop One Thing
routines.description: Once a week, choose one thing you'll let go of so the week has more room.
routines.parentGoal: Keep the week realistic by deciding ahead what doesn't need doing.
routines.childOutcome: A less stretched parent has more patience for the moments that matter.
steps: Look at the week ahead and list what's on your plate.
Pick one thing to skip, simplify, or hand to someone else.
Tell your partner or write it down so it actually happens.
